newsitem.title: USA: Physicians Resource hopeful on purchase plan.
newsitem.headline: Physicians Resource hopeful on purchase plan.

text.p: Physicians Resource Group Inc said on Wednesday it would use its new cash and note acquisition plan until its share price improved and it was confident the plan would gain acceptance over time.
Physicians Resource President Richard Owen told a Dillon Read anlyst meeting the company used to pay a combination of 80 percent stock and 20 percent cash when it bought physicians' practices.
But because of the decline in Physicians Resource's stock price over the past six to nine months, it was now paying 50 percent cash and 50 percent in convertible notes for acquisitions, he said.
On Tuesday the company said this acquisition program, while meeting with some acceptance in the market, was coming along slower than expected and was resulting in smaller acquisitions.
"We just started a cash and note program," Owen said. "It has been accepted and we've closed a number of acquisitions. The acceptance has been slower than anticipated but we expect that to change."
Owen said Physicians Resource would continue to use the cash and note program until the share price improved. He declined to comment on the outlook for the company's 1997 earnings.
Dillon Read analyst James Lane said his 1997 estimate for Physicians Resource was $0.63 per share compared to $0.75 per share in 1996.
